notes: A running account of where things stand by these headlines, revised after each edition rather than added to. Every version is kept.
Written by the model from the narratives, not from the headlines. It is a reading, not a record.
standing: US petrol, diesel and jet fuel prices have risen days before the midterms despite Donald Trump's promise to cut energy costs, Turkey has raised its special consumption tax on petrol and diesel, and US-Iran talks are reported stuck on two conflicting demands as Iran's Supreme Leader orders the military to readiness. Intel's 29% fall and a Taiwanese paper asking whether the AI bubble had burst sit beside reports of 700 Micron staff in Taiwan receiving five years' salary and Chinese third-quarter results led by AI computing; no Taiwanese state buying was reported on 1 November. France deployed 70,000 security personnel for a third weekend of rallies, Toulouse diverted metro and bus lines, and German coverage asked whether France's violence would reach Germany's Gen Z protest. In Poland the president and Donald Tusk's government are fighting over the Constitutional Tribunal, with protesters detained, while in India a case is filed against Mallikarjun Kharge and investigators wait for Azam Khan's release. Russia, the US vote counts, drones, Brazil and the Urda collision had no narrative today.
moved: The Iran and fuel thread turned from relief to revenue: on 31 October governments were cutting fuel and sales taxes, and on 1 November Turkey raised its fuel tax while US pump prices were reported up against Trump's promise, days before the midterms.

The AI spending thread dropped Taiwan's state buying, which no headline reported on 1 November, and was read instead as gains landing on a few chip and computing makers, with Micron's Taiwan staff payout and Chinese results led by AI computing.

The protest thread, revived by the Chronicle on 31 October, was carried forward by the edition itself on 1 November: 70,000 French security personnel for a third weekend, diverted transport in Toulouse and no negotiation reported.
A new thread began on constitutions and courts as the ground of political fights, led by Poland's dispute over the Constitutional Tribunal.
silent: Former leaders between courts and amnesty, begun on 29 October, has gone three editions without a narrative and is silent. Azam Khan's case returned on 1 November inside the new constitutions thread, so the subject may be continuing under a wider join rather than ending.

Failed safety systems and operator blame, begun on 29 October and tentative from the start, is silent after three editions. It was a loose join with only two stated causes, and its absence is as likely the weakness of the join as the world moving on.
Brazil's election and the United States has had no narrative since the evening of 27 October and nothing from Brazil appeared on 31 October or 1 November.
The rites thread did not return on 1 November, All Saints' Day, though its own narrative had pointed to these days; that is more likely the collection's sample than an absence of observance.

threads.label: Iran war, oil prices, taxes and wages
threads.text: On 26 October the join was the Gulf running talks and strike preparations side by side; on 27 October it was the Hormuz shock at the pump, then jet fuel, asphalt and subsidies. On 29 October it reached mortgage rates; on 30 October reports ran towards easing; on 31 October Brent rose to $117.64 and the price rise reached Italian inflation, pay rounds and tax relief. On 1 November no wage talks appeared. US petrol, diesel and jet fuel prices were reported up days before the midterms despite Trump's promise, Turkey raised its special consumption tax on fuel, the reverse of the cuts of the day before, and US-Iran talks stalled as Iran's military was ordered to readiness. The edition's case against says Turkey raises fuel taxes routinely and the rise may not answer the war.
threads.direction: It has spread from the pump to borrowing, wages and tax policy, and on 1 November turned to which governments carry the price and which take more of it as revenue.

threads.label: Brazil's election and the United States
threads.text: On 26 October Brazil's vote was read as a script in Buenos Aires, Madrid and Nairobi. On the morning of 27 October Trump called the election rigged; by that evening, after Lula's run-off win, the United States was the common party in Flávio Bolsonaro's exit, Lula's warning of persecution, about 300 US soldiers in Colombia and Machado's return to Venezuela. Its events then ran under wider joins: Flávio Bolsonaro's arrival in the United States and an amnesty plan for Jair Bolsonaro on 29 October, and Flávio's letter declaring himself president on 30 October. Nothing from Brazil appeared on 31 October or 1 November.
threads.direction: It moved from how Brazil's vote is read abroad to Washington's part in what follows, then was taken up under wider joins and fell silent.

threads.label: AI companies' listing, land and lawsuits
threads.text: On 26 October the join was an AI company listing the end of the world as a risk factor in its prospectus and the market buying the shares. Early on 27 October an edition followed data centres to county level, where land, grid and water requests were refused, and that morning Anthropic filed for a record US share listing as Elvis Presley's rights holders sued it over 200 songs. Data centres split into their own thread on 29 October. No narrative on listings or lawsuits has followed in five editions; the falls of Alphabet and Intel from 30 October to 1 November were carried in the AI spending thread.
threads.direction: It went from the prospectus to the ground and the courts, then fell silent as its market side was carried under the AI spending thread.

threads.label: Young people's protests and their policing
threads.text: On 26 October the join was young people in public squares; on 27 October students struck or occupied buildings in France, Mexico, India and Italy. After three silent editions the Chronicle revived it on 31 October, when protests called for the same weekend met a ban in La Rochelle, perimeters in Rochefort and Saintes and negotiation in Lisbon. On 1 November the edition itself carried the link forward: France deployed 70,000 security personnel for a third weekend of rallies, Toulouse diverted metro and buses, German coverage asked whether France's violence would reach its Gen Z protest, and protesters were detained in Poland over the Constitutional Tribunal. No headline reported a negotiation or a demand. That France was on its third weekend suggests the collection missed the first two.
threads.direction: It has moved from youth as a political image to student strikes and now to policing reported as officers counted and routes diverted, with the protesters' demands unreported.

threads.label: State housing drives and housing protests
threads.text: On the morning of 27 October one narrative joined Egypt, Indonesia and Tamil Nadu expanding housing through states and employers with Portugal investigating police conduct at housing protests, and the part property funds play. No narrative has followed it in five editions. Mortgage rates appeared in the oil thread on 29 and 30 October, and on 31 October Lisbon's housing camps and the Rossio demonstration appeared in the protest thread.

threads.label: Public schemes passing costs to households
threads.text: Begun on the evening of 27 October. In six countries a public scheme meant to cover a cost was reported as falling short: Canadians paying for private surgery from savings and GoFundMe, German adult children billed for parents' care, Lucknow's subsidised generic pharmacies short of medicines, a Bangladeshi antivenom programme lacking funds, compensation claims from 50,000 Australians over unlawful Centrelink suspensions, and doubt over a Mexican voluntary pension scheme. The case against noted that several of these stories have run for years. No narrative has carried it in the four editions since.

threads.label: AI-made faces and files in checks
threads.text: Begun on the evening of 27 October. Nigeria's electoral commission is investigating suspected AI-generated photos in the voters' register, New Zealand job seekers report being ignored as AI-written applications flood employers, an Australian court passed the first sentence under deepfake laws without jail, and fashion models face AI copies of their image. The join is that a plausible picture or document now costs little to make while checking it still takes a person's time. No narrative has carried it in the four editions since.

threads.label: Broadcasts and films removed over offence
threads.text: Begun on the evening of 27 October. A Chinese platform dropped Racing-Real Madrid and La Liga broadcasts were suspended after a remark by Mbappé, an Indian court ordered a documentary on Adani and Modi taken down, a Korean drama faced calls to halt over a Gwangju episode, and Neil Young sued to stop Trump rallies using his songs. Three of the headlines were the same Mbappé story. No narrative has carried it in the four editions since.

threads.label: AI spending: profit, sell-off and who gains
threads.text: Begun on 29 October with Samsung and CHPT profits on data centre demand beside Norwegian, Finnish and Russian disputes. On 30 October it reached US growth of 3.4% credited to AI investment and the results of Amazon and Alphabet. On 31 October Alphabet had its biggest fall on record, Intel lost 29% and Taiwan's state funds and central bank bought against record foreign selling. On 1 November no state buying was reported; the edition read the same falls as AI money landing narrowly, with 700 Micron staff in Taiwan reported paid five years' salary, Chinese third-quarter results led by AI computing, and robots sold as guards in Jiangsu and used by Ukrainian units. Its case against says the Chinese results may show spending spreading, not concentrating. No planning dispute has appeared since 29 October.
threads.direction: It has moved from profit and local objection to national growth and a share sell-off, and on 1 November to how few firms the spending reaches.

threads.label: Former leaders between courts and amnesty
threads.text: Begun on 29 October. South Korea's special counsel again sought, and by one report won, a death sentence for former president Yoon Suk Yeol over his martial law declaration, while in Brazil Alcolumbre planned an amnesty for Jair Bolsonaro and Flávio Bolsonaro reached the United States with Trump's consent. Spain's Zapatero, India's Azam Khan and Indonesia's anti-corruption law also appeared. No narrative carried the court cases on 30 or 31 October or 1 November, and it is now silent; Azam Khan's release reappeared on 1 November in the new constitutions and courts thread.

threads.label: Failed safety systems and operator blame
threads.text: Begun on 29 October and marked tentative by its own edition. A high-speed collision near Urda in Spain, which other headlines say killed 68 people, followed at least 15 warnings about faulty signalling; a JR train in Japan overran a station when its driver was drowsy and its automatic braking did not act; Bangladesh, Manila's airport and Mexico's networks had failures of grids, servers, cameras and internet. Only the Spanish and Japanese cases had a stated cause. No narrative has carried it in the three editions since, and it is now silent.

threads.label: Vote counts and rolls as contested ground
threads.text: Begun on 30 October. Flávio Bolsonaro released a letter declaring himself president of Brazil and then left the country; Gadi Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu of trying to delegitimise Israel's result; in the United States a federal inquiry into the Alaska vote is widening and Texas's attorney general is suing Houston's county clerk; in Delhi BJP booth agents filed deletion forms against Muslim voters; and a governorship in Imo, Nigeria, is disputed. No narrative carried it on 31 October or 1 November. On 1 November US fuel prices before the midterms appeared in the oil thread and Poland's tribunal fight in the new constitutions thread. One more edition without it turns it silent.

threads.label: Drones in war, numbers and arms production
threads.text: On 26 October one narrative joined drones cutting power, guarding a lake, carrying the wounded and being sold. After three silent editions drones returned on 30 October as a matter of numbers: a shortage of Ukrainian interceptors, a record raid shutting Moscow and St Petersburg airports, Finnish anti-drone training, Ukrainian loans to arms makers and Lithuanian conscription from 2032. The revival was the Chronicle's judgment. No narrative carried drones on 31 October or 1 November; Washington's 500 Patriot missiles for Ukraine went to the Russia thread, and Ukrainian units giving dangerous tasks to combat robots appeared in the AI thread on 1 November. One more edition without it turns it silent.
threads.direction: It has moved from the drone's many uses to the number of drones and the factories and conscripts states are raising to match them.

threads.label: Russia shunned by Europe, courted elsewhere
threads.text: Begun on 31 October. European ministers refused to stand beside Sergei Lavrov for the G20 photograph and Poland's foreign minister told him 'enough', while US and Russian foreign ministers discussed coordination at APEC, Washington weighed lifting sanctions on a Putin associate, Russia signed 53 documents at its Africa summit and Nigeria moved to replace a 1967 air agreement with Moscow. Washington also approved 500 Patriot missiles for Ukraine. The case against says the Europeans still attended and the African deals renew old ties. No narrative carried it on 1 November; its expectations, a US easing of sanctions and a European objection to one, are still open.

threads.label: Constitutions and courts as political battleground
threads.text: Begun on 1 November and marked tentative by its own edition. In Poland the president and Donald Tusk's government fight over control of the Constitutional Tribunal, with tensions outside the building and protesters detained; Egypt's Masrawy asks whether the constitution should be amended; a Portuguese column says Madeira should not wait for the national constitutional revision; and in India a case is filed against Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge over remarks about Modi while the Enforcement Directorate waits at the jail for Azam Khan's release. Its case against says only Poland's is a crisis and the rest may be ordinary. It sits near the silent former-leaders thread, which carried Azam Khan on 29 October, and the contested-count thread, though the narrative cited neither.

threads.label: Money leaving and states offering discounts
threads.text: Early on 27 October one narrative joined savings and fortunes moving into dollars, gold and trusts with states answering by amnesties and discounts meant to bring the money back into view. No narrative in the six editions since has followed it, so it stands as a single observation. The amnesty bills of 29 October concerned convictions, not tax or hidden money.

threads.label: AI buyouts and dangerous manual work
threads.text: Early on 27 October one narrative set office workers being paid to leave as AI takes their tasks against labourers still dying in ditches, fields and collapsed buildings. No later narrative has carried it in six editions. On 1 November the AI thread touched nearby ground, with Micron staff payouts in Taiwan and robot guards in Jiangsu said to replace five people, but no narrative revived this join.

threads.label: Rites counted before the days of the dead
threads.text: Early on 27 October one narrative joined reports that measured the rites of late October and early November before they happen: numbers of hosts, incense sticks, costumes and the strain on worshippers' knees. No narrative has carried it in the six editions since. On 31 October the only trace of Halloween was the cost of sweets inside the wage narrative, and on 1 November, All Saints' Day, no narrative returned to it.

threads.label: European household readiness and borrowed deterrence
threads.text: Early on 27 October one narrative joined European advice that households should be able to last 72 hours on their own with European states seeking cover from nuclear warheads they do not own. No narrative in the six editions since has returned to it. Finnish anti-drone training and Lithuanian conscription on 30 October went to the drones thread, and Europe's stance towards Russia on 31 October to its own thread.

threads.label: One football night watched worldwide
threads.text: On 26 October one narrative joined coverage of a single football night that drew attention across many countries at once. It was tied to one event and no narrative has carried it in the seven editions since. Football returned on 27 October only as a broadcasting dispute in the removal-over-offence thread.

threads.label: Courts re-sentencing past events
threads.text: On 26 October one narrative joined courts re-sentencing events of 1979 and 1996 with a library removing material from 2026, treating them as revisions of the record. No narrative has carried it in the seven editions since. The former-leaders, contested-count and constitutions threads touch nearby ground, but none re-sentences an old event.

withdrawn.held: AI companies' share listings, the copyright suit against Anthropic and county refusals of data centre land, grid and water formed one thread.
withdrawn.undone: On 29 October data centres returned on their own, as profit for Samsung and CHPT and as planning and security disputes in Norway, Finland and Russia, with no listing or lawsuit in view. The land and power question is running apart from the companies' finance and courts, so the merge no longer holds.

withdrawn.held: The Iran war's price rise was moving outward from the pump to central bank rates and loan contracts, with the war named less often at each step.
withdrawn.undone: On 30 October the reports ran the other way: Washington pressing Kyiv to stop hitting Russian refineries and sending Tehran a peace proposal, Israel's pump price set to fall, Russia budgeting on $50 oil and US mortgage rates down for two weeks. The war was named directly again, and the costs were reported as easing more than spreading.

withdrawn.held: The data centre question was running apart from the AI companies' finance, as a matter of land, power and security.
withdrawn.undone: On 30 October the data centre thread itself turned to finance: US growth credited to AI investment, Amazon's spending and Alphabet's fall in market value, with no planning or security dispute in that edition. The split of threads stands, but the separation of data centres from company finance does not.

withdrawn.held: On 30 October the Iran war's costs had turned towards easing, with Washington pressing for a lower oil price before the midterms.
withdrawn.undone: On 31 October Brent rose 2.4% to $117.64, Italy's inflation reached 5.4% and the price rise was argued over in pay rounds and tax relief in several countries. The easing reading did not last a day, and the earlier withdrawal of the outward-spread reading now looks premature.

withdrawn.held: The AI share sell-off was moving towards losses partly taken on by Taiwanese public money, through its state funds and central bank.
withdrawn.undone: On 1 November no state buying was reported, and the same thread was read as AI money landing on a few chip and computing makers, with Micron staff payouts and Chinese results led by AI computing. The public-money reading rested on one edition and is not carried as the thread's direction.

caseAgainst: This Chronicle rests on eight editions over about 121 hours, still with none stamped 28 October, and no expectation set by any narrative has yet been kept or failed, so none of the live threads' directions has been tested against a later headline. Three of today's four narratives carry continuation links, and the brief that asks for continuity may produce them as much as the world does; the protest thread was revived by my judgment on 31 October and only then linked by the edition. The oil thread has been read as spreading, easing, spreading and now as a question of who pays in four consecutive versions, which may reflect which headlines each collection caught more than any change in the market; Turkey's tax rise may be routine indexation, as its own case against says. The AI narrative joins a share price, a payroll, a housing estate and a front line, and its Chinese evidence can be read the opposite way; I have withdrawn its previous direction after one edition. Protest-day headlines are nearly always about policing, and today's came from a Singapore wire, a regional French daily, DW's Swahili service and a broadcaster's feature; that France was on its third weekend shows the collection missed earlier ones. The constitutions thread is tentative and may be one Polish crisis drawing ordinary cases into its frame. My earlier versions led with the war, and I have led with it again.
line: On 1 November 2026, days before the US midterms, Turkey raises its fuel tax as US pump prices rise and Iran talks stall; France deploys 70,000 for youth rallies.
revision: The former-leaders and backup-systems threads are marked silent and a new thread on constitutions and courts was begun, leaving seven live. The Taiwan public-money reading of the AI thread is withdrawn, the oil thread's direction now turns on who carries the fuel price, and the standing was rewritten around fuel taxes before the midterms, concentrated AI gains, French policing and Poland's tribunal.
